sentences.text: I have job security for life, you know.

alts.text: My position is secure for the rest of my life.

sentences.note: **job security**는 '잘릴 걱정 없는 안정성'이에요. 직장이 안정적이라고 자랑하거나 농담할 때 씁니다. 끝에 붙은 **you know**는 '~거든' 하는 느낌을 줘요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 뭐, 내가 스페인까지 간 것도 아니잖아.
sentences.text: Well, it's not like I went to Spain.

alts.text: Come on, I didn't go to Spain or anything.
It is not as though I travelled all the way to Spain.

sentences.note: **it's not like**는 '~한 것도 아니잖아'예요. 별일 아니라고 변명할 때 씁니다. 별거 아닌 일로 뭐라고 하는 상대에게 받아칠 때 딱 맞아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그래서, 너도 이제 건강 엄청 챙기는 그런 사람 되는 거야?
sentences.text: So, you're going to be one of those healthy, healthy, healthy guys?

alts.text: Turning into a health nut now, huh?
Are you going to become one of those people who are extremely health-conscious?

sentences.note: **one of those**는 '그런 부류'라는 뜻이에요. 친구가 갑자기 바뀌었을 때 살짝 놀리듯 씁니다. 운동이나 식단에 빠진 사람은 **health nut**이라고도 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 글쎄, 별로 잘하고 있는 것 같진 않은데.
sentences.text: Well, you're not doing a very good job.

alts.text: I am afraid you are not doing it very well.

sentences.note: 상대가 '나 지금 노력하는 중이야'라고 할 때 비꼬듯 받아치는 말이에요. **not doing a very good job**은 '잘 못하고 있다'를 돌려 말합니다. 짧게 받아칠 때는 **Could've fooled me**(전혀 그렇게 안 보이는데)라고도 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이 안약 하루에 세 번씩 일주일 동안 넣으세요. 그러면 금방 멀쩡해질 거예요.
sentences.text: I want you to take these drops three times a day for a week and you'll be as good as new.

alts.text: Three times a day for a week with these drops, and you're good.
Please use these drops three times daily for one week, and you will be completely recovered.

sentences.note: **as good as new**는 아프거나 고장 났던 것이 원래대로 멀쩡해졌다고 할 때 씁니다. 사람한테도 물건한테도 씁니다. **I want you to**는 의사나 선생님이 해야 할 일을 부드럽게 일러 줄 때 자주 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이런 식으로 알게 해서 정말 미안해.
sentences.text: I'm so sorry that you had to find out this way.

alts.text: Sorry you found out like this.
I sincerely apologize that you had to learn about it in this manner.

sentences.note: **find out**은 몰랐던 사실을 알게 된다는 뜻입니다. **had to find out this way**는 내 입으로 먼저 말했어야 할 일을 상대가 다른 데서 알게 됐을 때 사과하는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 지난 10년 동안 나한테 있었던 좋은 일들, 너 아니었으면 하나도 없었을 거야.
sentences.text: None of the amazing things that have happened to me in the last 10 years would have happened if it wasn't for you.

alts.text: All the great stuff from the last ten years? Wouldn't have happened without you.
Without you, none of the wonderful things that have happened to me over the past ten years would have been possible.

sentences.note: **if it wasn't for you**는 누군가에게 진심으로 고맙다고 할 때 쓰는 말입니다. 문법책에는 were로 나오지만 실제 말에서는 wasn't도 많이 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 어, 사실 이름은 두 개로 좁혀 놨어.
sentences.text: Uh, actually we we've narrowed it down to two names.

alts.text: We're down to two names, actually.
We have actually reduced our choices to two names.

sentences.note: **narrowed it down to**는 여러 후보 중에서 몇 개로 추렸을 때 씁니다. 아기 이름, 이사 갈 집, 저녁 먹을 식당을 고를 때 자주 나옵니다. 더 편하게는 **We're down to**라고 합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends
